mainTopic: Priorities between תלמוד תורה, עבודה, מקרא מגילה and מת מצוה, and רבי יהושע בן לוי's rules defining a כרך
overview: This עמוד first finishes a challenge to בית רבי, who said עבודה comes before תלמוד תורה. The angel who rebuked יהושע came because Torah study was neglected. The גמרא answers that Torah study of the רבים is greater than עבודה, but Torah study of a יחיד is less. It then challenges this from רבה בר הונא, who says festive-day mourning limits do not apply for a deceased תלמיד חכם. The גמרא answers that this rule proves the כבוד תורה of an individual, not the value of his study. Next, רבא ranks מצוות: מקרא מגילה comes before עבודה and תלמוד תורה, and a מת מצוה comes before both, learned from the word ״וּלְאַחוֹתוֹ״. He then asks whether מגילה or מת מצוה comes first, and answers that the מת מצוה wins because of כבוד הבריות. Finally, the גמרא studies rulings of רבי יהושע בן לוי about a כרך. These cover places near it or seen from it, a wall built after settling, the need for ten local בטלנין, and a city emptied of its בטלנין and then resettled. Another of his rulings begins at the end of the עמוד and continues on the next one.

steps.title: Torah study outweighs the daily offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its challenge. It reads the יהושע story as showing that the angel rebuked יהושע for neglecting Torah study. It cites רב שמואל בר אוניא that תלמוד תורה is greater than offering the תמידין, which contradicts the view that עבודה comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse teaches that יהושע spent the night deep in הלכה, studying Torah. And רב שמואל בר אוניא said: Torah study is greater than offering the daily sacrifices, as the angel said, 'Now I have come.' So how can anyone say עבודה is more important than Torah?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its challenge. The angel's rebuke and רב שמואל בר אוניא's statement both show that Torah study is greater than Temple service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The angel said 'Now I have come,' meaning 'now,' about the neglect of Torah study, and not about the missed תמידין. יהושע fixed this by spending the night in the 'depth' (עמק) of הלכה. This directly clashes with בית רבי's teaching that עבודה takes precedence over תלמוד תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: The depth of הלכה. This is a play on the word עֵמֶק (valley) in the verse.
'Now I have come.' These are the angel's words to יהושע (יהושע ה:יד).

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. It is the end of a challenge that began on the previous עמוד. The point is to contradict בית רבי, who said עבודה is more important than Torah study.

phrases.english: This teaches that he spent the night in the depth of halacha.
phrases.notes: This is learned from the פסוק 'וילן יהושע... בתוך העמק'.

phrases.english: And Rav Shmuel bar Unya said:

phrases.aramaic: גָּדוֹל תַּלְמוּד תּוֹרָה יוֹתֵר מֵהַקְרָבַת תְּמִידִין,
phrases.english: Torah study is greater than offering the daily sacrifices,
as it says: 'Now I have come'!

steps.triggerLanguage: גָּדוֹל תַּלְמוּד תּוֹרָה יוֹתֵר מֵהַקְרָבַת תְּמִידִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge begun earlier against בית רבי's ruling that עבודה takes precedence.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית רבי's view that עבודה takes precedence over תלמוד תורה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Scripture and רב שמואל בר אוניא rank Torah study above the תמידין, so Torah study should take precedence over עבודה.

steps.title: Torah study of the many versus of an individual
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. Torah study of the רבים, as in יהושע's case, outranks עבודה. Torah study of a יחיד ranks below עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not a problem. The יהושע story is about the Torah study of a whole community. The teaching of בית רבי is about the Torah study of a single person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by splitting Torah study into two kinds: community study and individual study.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהושע was studying with all of Israel, so that study outweighs the תמידין. When a single person studies alone, עבודה takes precedence. Both teachings stand, because they apply to different cases.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. This is the standard opening of an answer.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This refers to the Torah study of the many, and that refers to the Torah study of an individual.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא דְּרַבִּים, וְהָא דְּיָחִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case distinction: the two sources address different cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Torah study is a single category, so the two sources truly conflict.
steps.terutzMaskana: Torah study of רבים is greater than עבודה. Torah study of a יחיד is less than עבודה.

steps.title: Is an individual's Torah really minor? A משנה about mourning on festive days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the answer by asking whether an individual's Torah is really a light matter. It sets up its proof by quoting a משנה. The משנה lists which mourning practices women may do on חול המועד, and which they may do on ראש חודש, חנוכה and פורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is an individual's Torah study really a light matter? We learned in a משנה: on חול המועד, women may chant laments for the dead together, but they may not clap their hands in grief. רבי ישמעאל says: women close to the bier may clap. On ראש חודש, חנוכה and פורים, they may both lament and clap. But on both kinds of days, they may not wail in call-and-response.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer that an individual's Torah is less important. Here it only quotes the background משנה; the actual point arrives in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This משנה sets out the normal rule: festive days limit how much women may mourn. חול המועד is the strictest, and the rabbinic days ראש חודש, חנוכה and פורים allow more. On all of them, call-and-response wailing is forbidden. This baseline is needed to see what is special about a תלמיד חכם in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: But did we not learn in a משנה? This introduces a challenge from a משנה.
Here it means חול המועד, the intermediate days of a festival.
They clap their hands in grief.
They wail in call-and-response: one woman leads and the others answer.
The bier that carries the deceased.

steps.confusionAlert: This משנה is not about Torah study at all. It only sets up the normal mourning limits, so the next step can show that a תלמיד חכם is an exception.

phrases.english: And is the Torah study of an individual a light matter?
But didn't we learn: on the intermediate festival days, women may lament in unison
but they may not clap their hands,
Rabbi Yishmael says:
If they were close to the bier, they may clap.
On New Moons, on Chanukah, and on Purim,
they may lament and clap;
but on both these and those, they may not wail responsively.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 2 that a יחיד's Torah study ranks below עבודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sets up a baseline of festive-day mourning limits. The next step shows these limits fall away for a תלמיד חכם, which reveals how great an individual's Torah is.

steps.title: No festive restrictions when a Torah scholar dies
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר הונא rules that the festive-day mourning limits do not apply when the deceased is a תלמיד חכם. This applies to חול המועד, and all the more so to חנוכה and פורים. This shows the great honor due to an individual's Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה בר הונא said: the restrictions of the festival do not apply in the presence of a deceased Torah scholar. All the more so, the restrictions of חנוכה and פורים do not apply.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the punchline of the challenge. When a single תלמיד חכם dies, we set aside even the festival's limits on mourning. That suggests one person's Torah is very important.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תלמיד חכם's Torah is personal Torah, yet it overrides the honor of חול המועד, which is a Torah-level festival. The rabbinic days חנוכה and פורים are all the more overridden. So how can the גמרא call a יחיד's Torah study 'light'? The answer to this question comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: The festival's mourning restrictions do not apply.
In the presence of a deceased Torah scholar

steps.confusionAlert: Here the תלמיד חכם is the person who died. The women mourning him may lament, clap, and even wail in call-and-response.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the הלכה that a תלמיד חכם's honor overrides the festive-day limits on mourning. It is the key evidence that challenges the רבים/יחיד distinction.

phrases.english: And Rabba bar Huna said:
There is no festival in the presence of a Torah scholar;
phrases.notes: Meaning: the mourning limits are lifted for him.

phrases.english: all the more so Chanukah and Purim.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר הוּנָא: אֵין מוֹעֵד בִּפְנֵי תַּלְמִיד חָכָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in step 3 by adding the exception for a תלמיד חכם to the משנה's rules.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 2 that a יחיד's Torah study is less weighty than עבודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If an individual scholar's honor overrides even חול המועד, then individual Torah is very weighty, which contradicts calling it 'light'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Festive-day mourning restrictions are lifted for a deceased תלמיד חכם, and all the more so on חנוכה and פורים.

steps.title: Honoring Torah is different from studying Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from רבה בר הונא. That ruling shows that the honor of an individual's Torah is weighty. It does not show that an individual's Torah study is weighty.
steps.simpleTranslation: You are talking about honoring the Torah. Honoring the Torah of an individual is serious. But an individual's Torah study is light.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the challenge from step 4. The case of the deceased תלמיד חכם is about honor, not about learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge mixed up two different things: respect owed to a Torah scholar, and the value of one person's learning. The mourning rule proves only the first. So the answer from step 2 still stands: a יחיד's Torah study ranks below עבודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Honor shown to the Torah, and to those who carry it
You are saying / you are talking about

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying an individual's learning is unimportant. It means only that, when it clashes with עבודה, it ranks lower.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two separate measures. כבוד תורה of an individual is חמור. תלמוד תורה of an individual is קל compared with עבודה.

phrases.english: You are speaking of the honor of the Torah.
The honor of an individual's Torah is weighty;
but the Torah study of an individual is light.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 4
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the mourning laws. The distinction from step 2 between רבים and יחיד stays in place.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof confused honoring Torah (כבוד) with the value of Torah study (תלמוד).

steps.title: Reading the מגילה comes before עבודה and Torah study
steps.stepSummary: רבא says it is obvious that מקרא מגילה takes priority over עבודה. He bases this on רבי יוסי בר חנינא. It also takes priority over תלמוד תורה, based on the practice of בית רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is obvious to me. Between עבודה and reading the מגילה, reading the מגילה comes first, as we learn from רבי יוסי בר חנינא. Between Torah study and reading the מגילה, reading the מגילה comes first, as we learn from what the house of רבי relied on.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new list of priorities. He starts with reading the מגילה, which beats both עבודה and Torah study.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier on the דף, רבי יוסי בר חנינא learned that כהנים and לוים stop their עבודה to hear the מגילה. The scholars of בית רבי relied on that teaching to stop learning for the מגילה. So מקרא מגילה outranks both.

keyTerms.meaning: The house / academy of רבי יהודה הנשיא

phrases.english: Rava said: It is obvious to me:
Temple service and reading the Megilla —
reading the Megilla takes priority,
from the teaching of Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina.
phrases.notes: He taught earlier on the דף that כהנים and לוים interrupt their service to hear the מגילה.

phrases.english: Torah study and reading the Megilla —
reading the Megilla takes priority,
from what the scholars of the house of Rabbi relied upon.
phrases.notes: They interrupted their learning to go hear the מגילה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new statement by רבא ranking מצוות against each other
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מקרא מגילה takes priority over both עבודה and תלמוד תורה.

steps.title: A מת מצוה comes before Torah study
steps.stepSummary: רבא continues: burying a מת מצוה takes priority over תלמוד תורה. A ברייתא proves this, since one stops learning to escort the dead and to escort a bride.
steps.simpleTranslation: Between Torah study and a מת מצוה, the מת מצוה comes first. As a ברייתא teaches: We stop Torah study to carry out the dead and to bring in a bride.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds the next item to his list. Caring for a מת מצוה beats Torah study.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says one stops learning even for an ordinary funeral. So for a מת מצוה, a body with no one else to bury it, learning certainly gives way.

keyTerms.meaning: A dead person with no one else to bury them, so the burial falls on whoever finds the body
Carrying out the dead for burial
Escorting a bride to her wedding

phrases.english: Torah study and a met מצוה —
the met מצוה takes priority,
from what is taught in a baraita:
We interrupt Torah study
to carry out a dead person,
and to bring in a bride.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's list of priorities
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מת מצוה takes priority over תלמוד תורה.

steps.title: A מת מצוה comes before עבודה
steps.stepSummary: רבא states that a מת מצוה also takes priority over עבודה. He learns this from the word ״וּלְאַחוֹתוֹ״.
steps.simpleTranslation: Between עבודה and a מת מצוה, the מת מצוה comes first, as we learn from ״וּלְאַחוֹתוֹ״, "and for his sister."
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the last item in his list. A מת מצוה beats even עבודה, and he points to a פסוק as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רבא only names the source in one word. The גמרא will now quote the ברייתא that explains how ״וּלְאַחוֹתוֹ״ teaches this.

keyTerms.meaning: "And for his sister" (במדבר ו:ז), a phrase in the laws of the נזיר

phrases.english: Temple service and a met מצוה —
the met מצוה takes priority,
from the phrase "or for his sister."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's list, now comparing מת מצוה with עבודה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מת מצוה takes priority over עבודה, learned from ״וּלְאַחוֹתוֹ״.

steps.title: Quoting the ברייתא on "and for his sister"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting the ברייתא behind ״וּלְאַחוֹתוֹ״. The extra word is needed for a case like this: a man is on his way to bring his קרבן פסח or to give his son a ברית מילה, and he hears that a relative died. One might think he should become impure for that relative.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: Why does the פסוק need to say "and for his sister"? Picture a man who was going to slaughter his קרבן פסח and to circumcise his son. Then he heard that a relative of his had died. One might think he should become impure for that relative...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting the source for step 8. It is setting up the proof, and the ברייתא's conclusion comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier פסוק already forbids a נזיר to become impure from any dead body. So "and for his sister" looks extra, and the ברייתא uses it to teach a new case. The case pits a relative's death against two major מצוות‎, פסח and מילה. This builds toward showing that only a מת מצוה, not a relative, overrides them.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the פסוק need to say this?

steps.confusionAlert: "יכול יטמא" is not the ruling. It is the mistaken first thought, the הוה אמינא, that the ברייתא is about to reject.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
"Or for his sister" — why does the verse need to say this?

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי שֶׁהָיָה הוֹלֵךְ לִשְׁחוֹט אֶת פִּסְחוֹ
phrases.english: Consider one who was going to slaughter his Paschal lamb
or to circumcise his son,
and he heard that a relative of his had died;
one might think he should become impure —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins quoting the source that רבא pointed to in step 8
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that a מת מצוה takes priority over עבודה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא expounding ״וּלְאַחוֹתוֹ״ (במדבר ו:ז) in the laws of the נזיר

steps.title: The extra word allows impurity for a מת מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes that a person on the way to a big מצוה may not become impure for his sister, but he must become impure for a מת מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You said: 'He shall not become impure.' One might think that just as he does not become impure for his sister, he also does not become impure for a מת מצוה. So the verse says 'or for his sister.' It is for his sister that he does not become impure, but he does become impure for a מת מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא from Step 9. It shows that even someone on his way to bring a קרבן פסח must stop and become impure to bury a מת מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a relative, the answer is 'לא יטמא'. He should not become impure, because his קרבן פסח or his son's מילה is more important. The word 'וּלְאַחוֹתוֹ' teaches that this applies only to his sister, who has others to bury her. A מת מצוה has no one else, so burying it overrides even the קרבן. This proves רבא's claim in Step 8 that מת מצוה comes before עבודה.

keyTerms.meaning: And for his sister (the word the ברייתא learns from)

steps.whatToRemember: מת מצוה overrides עבודה. Even someone going to bring his קרבן פסח must become impure to bury a מת מצוה.

phrases.english: You said: "He shall not become impure."
One might think: just as he does not become impure for his sister,
so too he does not become impure for a met מצוה
Therefore the verse says: "or for his sister."
It is for his sister that he does not become impure,
but he does become impure for a met מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in Step 9
steps.raayaObject: מת מצוה takes priority over עבודה

steps.title: Reading the מגילה or burying a מת מצוה: which comes first?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks which wins: מקרא מגילה, because it publicizes the miracle, or מת מצוה, because of human dignity.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: reading the מגילה and burying a מת מצוה, which of them comes first? Does reading the מגילה come first, because it spreads the news of the miracle? Or perhaps the מת מצוה comes first, because of human dignity?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now compares the two winners from his earlier rules. Both מקרא מגילה and מת מצוה beat עבודה and תלמוד תורה, so he asks which of them beats the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side has a strong reason. The מגילה has פרסומי ניסא, telling the world about the miracle. The מת מצוה has כבוד הבריות, the dignity of a person. רבא's earlier rules do not settle this, so it is a real question.

phrases.english: Rava asked:
Reading the Megillah and a met מצוה,
which of them takes precedence?

phrases.aramaic: מִקְרָא מְגִילָּה עֲדִיף מִשּׁוּם פַּרְסוֹמֵי נִיסָּא,
phrases.english: Does reading the Megillah take precedence because of publicizing the miracle,
or perhaps the met מצוה takes precedence
because of human dignity?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבא's priority rules by comparing the two top items
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which comes first when they conflict: מקרא מגילה or מת מצוה

steps.title: רבא answers: the מת מצוה comes first
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers his own question. מת מצוה wins, because כבוד הבריות can even push aside a Torah prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: After he asked, he answered it himself: the מת מצוה comes first. As the Master said: human dignity is so great that it pushes aside a לא תעשה in the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers his own question. Burying a מת מצוה comes before reading the מגילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is a known rule: כבוד הבריות can override a Torah לא תעשה. If human dignity can push aside a Torah prohibition, it can surely push aside reading the מגילה, which is a rabbinic מצוה. So פרסומי ניסא gives way to the dignity of the dead.

keyTerms.meaning: After he asked it, he then answered it himself
As the Master said (quoting a known teaching)

steps.whatToRemember: The order of priority is: מת מצוה, then מקרא מגילה, then עבודה and תלמוד תורה. The reason is כבוד הבריות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the practical הלכה that one stops even the מגילה reading to bury a מת מצוה.

phrases.english: After he raised the question, he then answered it:
The met מצוה takes precedence,
as the Master said:
Great is human dignity,
for it overrides a prohibition in the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מת מצוה comes first, because כבוד הבריות overrides even a לא תעשה

steps.title: Towns near or visible from a walled city count as that city
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the statement of רבי יהושע בן לוי. A כרך, and every place next to it or seen with it, is treated like the כרך.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the main topic. רבי יהושע בן לוי said: a walled city, and every place near it, and every place seen with it, is judged like the walled city.
steps.whatsHappening: The word 'גופא' tells us the גמרא is going back to a statement it quoted earlier, in order to study it on its own. The topic now changes back to which places read the מגילה on the fifteenth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A place near a כרך, or a place that can be seen from it, gets the law of the כרך. So it reads the מגילה on the fifteenth. The statement lists two ways to be included, closeness and visibility, but it does not yet say whether each one is enough alone.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself (going back to study a quoted statement)

phrases.aramaic: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: Returning to the matter itself: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
A walled city, and every place near it,
and every place that can be seen with it,
is judged like the walled city.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the priority discussion and returns to an earlier quoted statement
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Places near or visible from a כרך are treated like the כרך

steps.title: A teaching: each condition is enough by itself
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that a place counts if it is near, even when not seen, and also if it is seen, even when not near.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: a near place counts, even if it cannot be seen. A visible place counts, even if it is not near.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא explains רבי יהושע בן לוי's two conditions. Each one is enough on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You do not need both closeness and visibility. Being near is enough, and being visible is enough. This sets up the גמרא's next question about how these cases can happen.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read רבי יהושע בן לוי as requiring both conditions together. The ברייתא says either one alone is enough.

phrases.english: It was taught:

phrases.aramaic: סָמוּךְ — אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִרְאֶה,
phrases.english: A near place counts, even though it cannot be seen;

phrases.aramaic: נִרְאֶה — אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ סָמוּךְ.
phrases.english: a visible place counts, even though it is not near.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the two conditions in Step 13
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Closeness alone or visibility alone is enough

steps.title: How can a place be near but not seen?
steps.stepSummary: A visible but distant place is easy to picture, such as one on a mountaintop. But how can a place be close to the כרך yet not be seen from it?
steps.simpleTranslation: A place that is seen but not near makes sense. You find it when the place sits on top of a mountain. But a place that is near but not seen, how can that happen?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how one of the ברייתא's cases could happen in real life. This sets up רבי ירמיה's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A town on a mountaintop can be seen from far away, so 'seen but not near' is easy to picture. But anything close by would usually be visible. So the גמרא asks for a realistic case of 'near but not seen'.

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא נִרְאֶה אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ סָמוּךְ,
phrases.english: It makes sense that a place is seen though it is not near:

phrases.aramaic: מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ כְּגוֹן דְּיָתְבָה בְּרֹאשׁ הָהָר.
phrases.english: you find this when it sits on top of a mountain.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא סָמוּךְ אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִרְאֶה
phrases.english: But a place that is near though it is not seen,
how can you find such a case?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא נִרְאֶה אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ סָמוּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how a case from the ברייתא in Step 14 could happen
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A realistic case of a place that is near the כרך but not visible from it

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: a town in a valley
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה answers that the place sits in a valley, so it is close but hidden from view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: it is a place that sits in a valley.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה gives the real-life case the גמרא asked for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A town down in a valley can be very close to the כרך but still be hidden by the land around it. That is the case of 'near but not seen', and it still counts like the כרך.
steps.whatToRemember: A place counts like a כרך if it is near it (even if hidden in a valley) or if it can be seen from it (even if far, on a mountaintop).

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
Where it sits in a valley.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A town in a valley is close to the כרך but cannot be seen from it

steps.title: A city settled first and walled later counts as a village
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי rules that a כרך that was settled first and only later surrounded by a wall is treated like a כפר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע בן לוי said: A city that was settled and only later surrounded by a wall is judged like a village.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement of רבי יהושע בן לוי about which walled cities count as a כרך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order matters. A wall that was put up after people already lived there does not give the city כרך status. Such a city does not read the מגילה on the fifteenth like a כרך; it follows the rules of an unwalled place.

keyTerms.meaning: And in the end, only later
Is judged like a village (not a walled city)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
A city that was settled and only later walled
is judged like a village.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, separate statement of the same אמורא, whose earlier statement was discussed in Steps 13-16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A city whose wall came only after it was settled is treated as a כפר.

steps.title: The verse shows the wall must come before the settling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason, and proves the rule from the words 'בית מושב עיר חומה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because it is written: 'And if a man sells a house of dwelling in a walled city.' This means a city that was walled and then settled, and not one that was settled and then walled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule and brings a פסוק to prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'מושב עיר חומה' mean a place where people settled inside an existing wall. So the wall must already be there when the settling happens. If the people came first and the wall came later, it is not the 'עיר חומה' of the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: A dwelling house in a walled city (ויקרא כה:כט)

phrases.english: What is the reason?
As it is written: 'And if a man sells
a dwelling house in a walled city'
meaning one that was walled and then settled,
and not one that was settled and then walled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the Torah source for the ruling in Step 17.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a city settled before being walled is a כפר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא כה:כט, 'בית מושב עיר חומה', which describes settling inside an existing wall.

steps.title: A walled city without ten idlers counts as a village
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי rules that a כרך without ten בטלנין is treated like a כפר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע בן לוי said: A walled city that does not have ten idlers is judged like a village.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second new statement of רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בטלנין are people free from work who are always available for community needs, like making a מנין. Without ten of them, even a walled city loses its city status and is treated as a כפר.

keyTerms.meaning: People free from work who are available for community needs, such as a מנין

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
A walled city that does not have ten idlers
is judged like a village.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new statement of the same אמורא, on a different requirement (population, not walls).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כרך lacking ten בטלנין is treated as a כפר.

steps.title: Why say this if a משנה already teaches it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that a משנה already says a place with fewer than ten בטלנין is a כפר.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us? We already learned: What is a large city? Any city that has ten idlers. Fewer than that, it is a village.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יהושע בן לוי by asking what his statement adds to a משנה that already says the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה (on 5a) already defines a large city by its ten בטלנין and calls anything less a כפר. So רבי יהושע בן לוי's statement looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? (What does this add?)

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
We already learned: What is a large city?
Any city that has ten idlers.
Fewer than that, it is a village. (So what is new?)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether Step 19 adds anything new.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for רבי יהושע בן לוי's statement in Step 19.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה already teaches that fewer than ten בטלנין makes a place a כפר, so his statement seems redundant.

steps.title: The new point: visitors from outside do not count
steps.stepSummary: The statement was needed for a כרך, to teach that idlers who come from elsewhere do not make up the ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needed to teach it about a walled city: even though people happen to come there from the outside world, it is still a village.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהושע בן לוי is adding a new detail about a כרך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A big walled city often has many visitors passing through, so one might think they fill the ten. רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that only local בטלנין count. Visitors from outside do not.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary for him (to say it)
That people happen to come to it from the outside world

phrases.english: He needed it for a walled city,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּמִיקַּלְעִי לֵיהּ מֵעָלְמָא.
phrases.english: even though people happen to come there from elsewhere.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 20 by showing a new point.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a new case not covered by the משנה (a כרך with outside visitors).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Visitors who keep coming to a כרך might count toward the ten בטלנין.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only local בטלנין count. A כרך without ten local ones is a כפר, even if visitors come.

steps.title: A destroyed walled city that is resettled counts as a walled city
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי rules that a כרך that was חרב and later resettled is treated like a כרך.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע בן לוי said: A walled city that was destroyed and later settled again is judged like a walled city.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third statement of רבי יהושע בן לוי. It sets up a question about what 'destroyed' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling says that once the city is lived in again, it gets back its כרך status. The unclear word is 'חרב', which the גמרא will examine next.

keyTerms.meaning: Is judged like a walled city

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
A walled city that was destroyed and later settled
is judged like a walled city.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third, separate statement of the same אמורא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כרך that was חרב and then resettled is treated as a כרך.

steps.title: 'Destroyed' cannot mean the walls fell
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries reading 'חרב' as 'its walls fell', but a ברייתא of רבי אליעזר בר יוסי shows a city keeps its walled status even without its walls.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'destroyed' mean? If you say its walls were destroyed, then the rule would be: if it was resettled, yes it is a walled city, and if not, no. But a ברייתא teaches that רבי אליעזר בר יוסי says: 'which has [written: has no] a wall' teaches that even if it has no wall now, if it had one before, it counts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what 'destroyed' means. It tests one reading, 'the walls fell', and attacks it with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'חרב' meant the walls fell, רבי יהושע בן לוי would be saying the city counts only once resettled. But רבי אליעזר בר יוסי learns that a city that once had a wall keeps its status even with no wall now. Resettling would not matter at all, so this reading must be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a reading that will be rejected)
But was it not taught in a ברייתא?
Written with an א ('no'), but read as לו ('it has')

steps.confusionAlert: The word לוֹא is spelled like 'no' (לא) but read as 'it has' (לו). רבי אליעזר בר יוסי uses both. It has no wall now, yet it counts as having one, because it had a wall before.

phrases.english: What does 'destroyed' mean?
If you say its walls were destroyed,
then if settled, yes; if not settled, no?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בַּר יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: But it was taught: Rabbi Eliezer bar Yosei says:
'Which has [written: has no] a wall'

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ עַכְשָׁיו
phrases.english: teaches: even though it has none now,
if it had one before, it counts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the key word in Step 22 means, and rejects the first possible reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading 'חרב' in Step 22 as 'its walls were destroyed'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says a city that once had a wall keeps its status without the wall. Resettling would then be irrelevant to wall status, so that cannot be what רבי יהושע בן לוי meant.

steps.title: 'Destroyed' means it lost its ten idlers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that 'חרב' means the city lost its ten בטלנין. Once it has ten again, it is a כרך again.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does 'destroyed' mean? That it was emptied of its ten idlers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct meaning of 'destroyed' and resolves the problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects back to the second statement (Step 19). A כרך without ten בטלנין is a כפר. Once it is resettled with ten, it returns to being a כרך, and its old wall still counts.
steps.whatToRemember: Three rules of רבי יהושע בן לוי: (1) The wall must come before the settling. (2) A כרך needs ten local בטלנין, and visitors do not count. (3) A כרך that lost its ten בטלנין becomes a כרך again once it has them back. Losing the wall itself does not cancel its status.

phrases.english: Rather, what does 'destroyed' mean?
That it was emptied of its ten idlers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא of Step 23 by redefining 'חרב'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the key term in the statement.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'חרב' means the city lost its ten בטלנין. When resettled with ten, it is again a כרך.

steps.title: Introducing another ruling of רבי יהושע בן לוי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens another statement from רבי יהושע בן לוי. The content of the ruling follows in the next part of the text.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע בן לוי said:
steps.whatsHappening: This is only a setup line. The גמרא is announcing that another teaching from רבי יהושע בן לוי is about to be quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'and' (וְ) shows that this new statement is part of a series. The גמרא has just explained one of his rulings about a כרך, and now it adds another ruling from him on the same general topic. Nothing is ruled yet; the actual teaching comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: And he said. This links a new statement to the one just discussed.
Said. The standard word that introduces an אמורא's statement.
A major early אמורא of ארץ ישראל. Several rulings in this sugya come from him.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not look for a ruling in this line. It is only the introduction. The content of his statement starts on the next עמוד.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: Setup/attribution line for the next מימרא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After resolving the meaning of 'חרב' in his previous ruling (Steps 22-24), the גמרא introduces another teaching from the same רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling is stated on this amud. It only introduces a new statement of רבי יהושע בן לוי, which follows next.
